prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: hit while turning left in Houston, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported wrist fracture. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1047; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text: Officer narrative. On arrival at the intersection in Houston, Texas, I observed a two-vehicle collision. Driver 1 reported that while turning left across oncoming traffic, Driver 2's vehicle struck the driver's side of Driver 1's vehicle. Driver 1 stated having sustained a wrist fracture and was transported for treatment. Driver 2 confirmed the sequence of events as described. Two independent witnesses and photographs taken at the scene are consistent with that account. The damage to both vehicles corresponds to the angle and force of the impact. Driver 1 was identified as a resident of the same household as the registered policyholder. Passenger, seated in the rear, was not injured. It could not be fully determined from the scene where Driver 1 was positioned in the vehicle at the moment of impact, as Driver 1 gave differing accounts when questioned. No prior damage to Driver 1's vehicle was observed or reported by any party. Both vehicles were removed from the roadway by tow.
